source.title: State transitions and momentum effect in cryptocurrency market

hypothesis: Short-horizon cross-sectional crypto momentum is profitable primarily when the aggregate crypto market remains in consecutive UP states; conditioning on causal UP-UP transitions should improve net Sharpe versus unconditional momentum.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain the 50 contracts with highest trailing 30-day quote volume among assets with exact causal history.
market_state: At each Monday, compute each eligible asset's return from the close 29 calendar days earlier to the prior completed Sunday close, then take a trailing-quote-volume-weighted cross-sectional mean. State is UP if this 4-week market return proxy is >=0. UP-UP requires both the current Monday state and the independently reconstructed prior Monday state to be UP.
signal: Prior completed F-day close-to-close return ending Sunday.
portfolio: When state is UP-UP, equal-weight long top momentum quintile / short bottom momentum quintile at 0.5 gross per side; otherwise cash.
execution: Features use data only through Sunday close; trade at Monday 00:00 UTC open and exit/rebalance next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical conditional mean rank IC >0.02, positive conditional winner-minus-loser next-week return, canonical net Sharpe >0.70, and >=2/3 formation windows positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0, positive at 2x costs, >=2/3 formation windows positive, 2024 and 2025 non-negative, max drawdown <35%, excluding BTC/ETH positive, and excluding strongest contributor positive.
source_deviation: The source uses CoinMarketCap value-weighted market returns. Historical point-in-time market cap is unavailable locally, so lagged trailing quote volume is pre-registered as the market-weight proxy. Formation horizons are preregistered because the accessible source establishes short weekly momentum but does not expose one exact winner-loser formation window.
